subject: Follow-up: FintechAI cost/pricing and latency trade-offs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T15:03:00Z
Subject: FintechAI — follow-up & pricing qualification

Hi Michael — great speaking earlier. Quick recap + two asks so we can scope a clear pilot and pricing proposal:

Recap from our call:
- Primary use case: realtime chat assistance inside your loan origination product (short prompts with dynamic context + retrieval).
- Expected ROI metric: reduce support handle time and increase conversion on approvals.
- Compliance drivers: data residency + SOC2 evidence requested.

Two asks (helps us give tight unit economics):
1) Monthly token volumes (rough bucket is fine). Please include current expected production volumes and 12-month ramp. e.g. 50M/month now, 200M/month in 12 months.
2) Target unit economics — what target $/1M tokens would make this project greenlit for you (ballpark is okay).

A few notes up front on latency vs cost trade-offs (short summary):
- Streaming (token-by-token) = best UX for chat (low time-to-first-token) but slightly higher served-cost due to less aggressive batching.
- Batching = reduces per-token compute cost (20–40% potential savings depending on workload) but adds queueing latency; good for high-throughput background jobs or non-time-sensitive completions.
- Dedicated/Committed capacity = lower unit cost (we can price ~15–35% below hosted rates depending on commit) + predictable latency; ideal if you have steady volumes and strict SLOs.

If you can send the two items above and any security questionnaire (SSO/SOC2), I’ll put together 2 pricing options for you: Hosted (streaming-first) and Dedicated (SLO-driven commit), plus an example of how batching/quantization might change unit cost.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

Michael — great, thanks for the detail and attachments. High-level response + concrete options (ballpark numbers to validate against your $150/1M target):

Assumptions:
- Workload: short chat responses, average 200 tokens per session; heavy small-payload retrieval context (prefix KV cache benefits).
- Volume scenarios: Pilot = 50M tokens/month; Ramp = 200M tokens/month.

Option A — Hosted API (streaming-first, minimal infra work) - Pros: fast to ship, streaming UX intact, no infra ops - Cons: higher per-token price vs commit - Estimated unit price (streaming, on-demand): $180 / 1M tokens (pilot). At 200M tokens/month we can offer usage tiers that push toward ~$160 / 1M tokens. Latency: p95 150–300ms typical depending on model/region and request size (should be able to meet 250ms in most cases).

Option B — Dedicated (reserved capacity, SLO-driven pricing) - Pros: predictable latency, lower unit cost, better for PII/compliance controls - Cons: commit required, slightly longer setup - Estimated pricing: with a modest monthly commit (example: 500M tokens/month commitment across the cluster) we can get to ~$110–130 / 1M tokens depending on burst profile and quantization choices. For your stated 200M target, a smaller commit (200–300M) would still move unit cost into the ~$130–150 / 1M range. Latency: p95 < 200–250ms achievable with dedicated pools and streaming enabled.

Option C — Cost-optimized batching + quantization (if you can accept higher tail latency) - Behavior: batch aggressively, allow slightly higher p95 (350–600ms) - Savings: 20–40% vs hosted streaming pricing depending on request distribution - When to pick: non-interactive flows or where p95 SLO is relaxed.

Quick recommendation for pilot:
- Start Hosted streaming pilot (50M) to validate quality/latency in prod flows.
- If 200M is realistic on ramp, evaluate a Dedicated commit to target ~$130 / 1M. We can structure a 3-month pilot PO + credit toward a dedicated commit if you convert.

Next steps I’ll take now:
- Share a short SLO-driven quote for 3 configurations: Hosted streaming (pilot), Dedicated small commit (200–300M), Dedicated larger commit (500M) — with rough $/1M numbers and expected p95 latency.
- Dylan (cc’d) will put together an SRE/ops note on how batching settings and streaming toggle change CPU/GPU utilization (helps procurement justify commit).

If that sounds right, I’ll turn this into a formal one-pager and a pricing sheet.

Best,
Marissa
